evals.prompt: Why is the Llama 2 70B parameters file 140 GB, and how much code does it take to run it?
evals.expected_output: 70B parameters x 2 bytes each (float16) = 140 GB; the run file can be about 500 lines of C with no dependencies.
expectations: Says each parameter is stored as 2 bytes / float16 (LLM Inference ~113s)
Says about 500 lines of C (LLM Inference ~143s)

evals.prompt: What did it take to pretrain Llama 2 70B?
evals.expected_output: About 10 TB of internet text, ~6,000 GPUs for ~12 days, about $2M, compressing to 140 GB of parameters (~100x, lossy).

evals.prompt: When is it worth using comparison labels (stage 3 / RLHF) rather than having labelers write ideal answers?
evals.expected_output: When comparing candidate answers is much easier than writing one, e.g. picking the best of several haikus about paper clips; this optional stage 3 is called RLHF at OpenAI.
expectations: Says comparing candidates is easier than generating an answer, with the haiku example (Appendix: Comparisons... ~1265-1296s)
Identifies this as RLHF / optional stage 3 (Appendix ~1327s)

evals.prompt: My deployed assistant misbehaves on some queries. According to Karpathy, how do you fix it, and why do companies iterate on this stage rather than pretraining?
evals.expected_output: Take the conversation where the assistant erred, have a person write the correct response, insert it into the fine-tuning data and fine-tune again; fine-tuning is far cheaper (about a day vs months) so it can be repeated weekly or daily, while pretraining happens maybe once a year.
expectations: Says a person overwrites the incorrect response and it is added to the fine-tuning data (Summary so far ~1164-1196s)
Says fine-tuning is much cheaper (~1 day) so companies iterate on it often, unlike pretraining (Summary so far ~1102-1196s)

evals.prompt: How did adding vision make LLMs both more capable and more attackable?
evals.expected_output: Capability: ChatGPT read Greg Brockman's pencil sketch of a joke website and wrote working HTML/JS. Attack surface: an image of a panda with optimized noise jailbreaks the model, and faint white text in an image can carry a prompt injection.
expectations: Mentions the adversarial panda-noise image jailbreak or image-borne prompt injection (Jailbreaks ~3050s / Prompt Injection ~3090s)

evals.prompt: Where in the talk does Karpathy discuss the 'reversal curse' (Tom Cruise's mother)?
evals.expected_output: Around 12:54 (774 s), in How do they work?
expectations: Gives a timestamp within 60 s of 774 s (How do they work?)
Describes it: GPT-4 knows Tom Cruise's mother is Mary Lee Pfeiffer but not who her son is (How do they work?)
